facts.statement: The study compared 20 patients with left temporal lobe epilepsy, 20 with right temporal lobe epilepsy, and 35 healthy controls while measuring their brain activity with EEG during a visual working memory task.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Both epilepsy groups made more errors and took longer to respond than the healthy control group.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Patients with right temporal lobe epilepsy responded more slowly than those with left temporal lobe epilepsy.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The right epilepsy group showed lower theta brain wave activity in the frontal and occipital areas compared to the left epilepsy group.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Measures of neural outflow were lower in the right epilepsy group than in the left epilepsy group.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Weakened information flow from the front of the brain to the parietal and temporal regions was associated with lower accuracy and slower responses.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors suggest that disrupted communication from the prefrontal cortex to the parietal lobe may cause working memory deficits, and that damage to connections with the right temporal gyri worsens these impairments.
facts.subject: humans
